ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe2-lieber-sally.name: Sally J. Lieber
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe2-lieber-sally.bio: Chair of the State Board of Equalization; former city councilmember, mayor, county commissioner, State Assemblymember, and Franchise Tax Board member.

positions.stance: Says state agencies must be transparent and accountable, enhancing available information and making it accessible and usable; is running a corporate-free campaign.
Wants the Board of Equalization fully staffed with highly trained personnel and future staff recruited through colleges and universities.
Will continue examining affordable-housing funding programs, ensure voter-approved housing funds are used wisely, and keep state tax credits "transparent, sustainable and fair."
Calls the climate crisis "an existential threat for California" and wants every government agency working toward sustainability, including greenbelt protection.
Commits to serving veterans, homeowners, seniors, people with disabilities, and small businesses through housing, services, and access to information.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe2-pimentel-john.name: John Pimentel
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe2-pimentel-john.bio: Former California Deputy Secretary for Transportation, community college trustee, and Menlo Park housing commissioner; clean energy and water infrastructure developer.

positions.stance: "End the sales tax on food," which he calls a regressive tax that burdens working families, seniors, and young people.
Close tax loopholes so large corporations and the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share, naming the Water's Edge Election, Invest/Borrow/Die, and carried interest.
Strengthen transparency and accountability so the Board of Equalization operates effectively and earns the public's trust.

tx-bexar-2026-da-foster-ashley.name: Ashley Foster
tx-bexar-2026-da-foster-ashley.bio: Former Bexar County assistant district attorney for 11 years who prosecuted thousands of felony cases.

positions.stance: Pledges not to accept donations from defense attorneys who practice before the Bexar County District Attorney's Office.
Will set clear charging standards, prioritize prosecution of the most dangerous offenders, and move serious felonies swiftly from filing to resolution.
Will put victims at the center with timely updates, trauma-informed advocacy, a single point of contact, and input in plea discussions and sentencing.
Will reduce the case backlog through streamlined intake, earlier discovery exchange, case triage, and published timelines and performance metrics.
Will launch a year-round training academy for prosecutors covering trial advocacy, evidence law, ethics, digital evidence, and trauma-informed practices.

tx-bexar-2026-da-chapa-luz-elena.name: Luz Elena Chapa
tx-bexar-2026-da-chapa-luz-elena.bio: Former justice on Texas's Fourth Court of Appeals (2013-2025) and licensed attorney for over 25 years.

positions.stance: Will ensure the DA's office is fully funded and fully staffed so prosecutors have the resources they need.
Will "work non-stop on behalf of victims of crime and advocate tirelessly for the most vulnerable."
Calls the backlog of unprosecuted domestic violence cases "a stain on Bexar County" and will make sure prosecutors are trauma-informed trained.
Will repair the relationship between the DA's office and law enforcement, rebuilding trust and cooperation.

tx-bexar-2026-district-clerk-castillo-ch.name: Christine "Chris" Castillo
tx-bexar-2026-district-clerk-castillo-ch.bio: Worked 33 years in the Bexar County District Clerk's office, including 20 years as a supervisor and 8 years as a division chief.

positions.stance: Says "We need to create transparency and accountability" in the District Clerk's office and promote open communication.
Wants to "assure e-filed documents are accepted promptly and efficiently."
Would complete the digitization project and enhance online accessibility, including online document viewing and copy purchases from home.
Would make accessibility, "especially for our underserved and vulnerable populations, a top priority."
Plans expedited and curbside services and bringing the District Clerk's office to neighborhoods on a regular rotation, plus satellite hubs.

tx-dallas-2026-cda-givens-amber.name: Amber Givens
tx-dallas-2026-cda-givens-amber.bio: Former judge who describes herself as a justice innovator and advocate.

positions.stance: Proposes an "Evidence-Ready Prosecution Standard" identifying all evidence at the start of each case, with structured 30-, 60-, and 90-day reviews.
Would create monthly Community Justice Councils of residents, faith leaders, advocates, and public safety partners to review case trends and shape recommendations.
Supports evidence-based diversion for youth, mental health, substance use, and first-time low-level offenses, saying "Smart justice is safer justice."
Would publish public policies on evidence disclosure, plea practices, grand jury standards, diversion eligibility, and victim communication timelines.

tx-dallas-2026-district-clerk-muehlhaeus.name: Dave Muehlhaeusler
tx-dallas-2026-district-clerk-muehlhaeus.bio: Retired mechanical engineer with 27 years of experience in product development, quality control, and data management.

positions.stance: Calls for "True digital records — not scanned images of handwritten documents" in the District Clerk's office.
Wants court forms and information available in both English and Spanish.
Wants every court event recorded with a specific, searchable code rather than an overused generic label.
Would mandate structured e-filing fields to eliminate handwritten scanned forms.
Would launch automated exception reporting dashboards to make the case backlog visible and accountable in real time.
Wants to restore trust by making every public record and administrative decision of the County Clerk's office easily accessible to all citizens.
Would streamline outdated processes with contemporary technology to reduce wait times, eliminate errors, and save taxpayer dollars.
Would expand outreach programs and ensure "language justice" for Dallas County's diverse population.

tx-dallas-2026-county-clerk-offord-damar.name: Damarcus L Offord
tx-dallas-2026-county-clerk-offord-damar.bio: Former senior staffer for Congresswoman Eddie Bernice Johnson, Dallas ISD intergovernmental relations leader, and senior manager of state relations at a Texas transportation agency.

tx-dallas-2026-treasurer-phelps-corsandr.name: Corsandra Brigham Phelps
tx-dallas-2026-treasurer-phelps-corsandr.bio: Licensed financial services representative for over 22 years.

positions.stance: Will push for public financial dashboards and easy-to-read reports showing exactly where taxpayer dollars go.
Will strengthen internal controls to prevent waste, fraud, or misuse and modernize treasury systems for accuracy, security, and speed.
Supports financial literacy workshops, taxpayer education, town halls, and outreach prioritizing underserved neighborhoods.

tx-dallas-2026-treasurer-medrano-pauline.name: Pauline Medrano
tx-dallas-2026-treasurer-medrano-pauline.bio: Dallas County Treasurer since 2015; former Dallas City Council member and Mayor Pro Tem.

tx-harris-2026-county-attorney-kamin-abb.name: Abbie Kamin
tx-harris-2026-county-attorney-kamin-abb.bio: Harris County Attorney and civil rights and general civil attorney; former Houston City Council member.

positions.stance: Will use lawsuits and "creative legal strategies" to block or slow actions by Donald Trump, Greg Abbott, and allies she says harm Harris County families.
Will use the office's full authority to protect voter access, defend election workers, and litigate against voter suppression and unlawful state interference in county elections.
Will partner with the District Attorney to expedite civil protective orders, refer abusers for prosecution, and expand resources for survivors.
Supports expanding violence-prevention and gun violence interruption programs and removing legal obstacles to them while ensuring accountability for serious harm.
Will push reforms in child and adult protective services cases so "the interests of the child are always put first," protecting parental rights when appropriate.

tx-harris-2026-district-clerk-daniel-chr.name: Chris Daniel
tx-harris-2026-district-clerk-daniel-chr.bio: Harris County District Clerk elected in 2010 and reelected in 2014; former Lone Star College System trustee and mechanical engineer.

tx-harris-2026-district-clerk-jordan-dar.name: Darrell Jordan, Jr
tx-harris-2026-district-clerk-jordan-dar.bio: Former Harris County Criminal Court at Law No. 16 judge and presiding judge; U.S. Army officer for over 24 years who heads the Texas Army National Guard's Trial Defense Services Office.

positions.stance: Would secure polling locations early, assess them for ADA compliance and security, recruit election workers early, and train poll workers on accessibility.
Would modernize property search tools, publish vital statistics processing timelines and annex wait times, and expand online filing and electronic certified copies.
Would publish quarterly performance metrics including processing times and backlog data.
Would hold quarterly stakeholder meetings with attorneys, publish e-filing rejection metrics, and standardize rejection notices with clear corrective guidance.
Would improve searchability of Commissioners Court records, hold quarterly public forums, and "Maintain professional administrative neutrality in all public communications."

tx-harris-2026-county-clerk-hudspeth-ten.name: Teneshia Hudspeth
tx-harris-2026-county-clerk-hudspeth-ten.bio: Harris County Clerk since 2020, previously chief deputy and other staff roles in the office since 2005.

tx-harris-2026-hcde-p5-davis-erica.name: Erica Davis
tx-harris-2026-hcde-p5-davis-erica.bio: Harris County Department of Education trustee since 2020 and former high school Spanish teacher.

positions.stance: Believes "safe schools are built on prevention, preparation, and relationships," not on how many metal detectors a campus has.
"Our children deserve support, not handcuffs. I'm committed to keeping kids in classrooms, not pushing them into courts."
Committed to an educational ecosystem where a child's zip code, race, language, disability, or family income never decides their future.
Would request a comprehensive zero-based budget review of all HCDE divisions within ninety days of taking her board seat.
Says every dollar must produce a measurable benefit for students; would eliminate DEI offices and contracts and rebid or drop underperforming vendor contracts.
Views HCDE's pooled special education services as cost-saving infrastructure and wants them run at the lowest cost per student while maintaining or improving quality.
Supports fully implementing SB 10's Ten Commandments displays and bringing SB 11 voluntary prayer periods to an early board vote.
Would publicly post all curriculum before approval, create a Parent Advisory Board with review authority, and require parental consent on gender identity discussions.

fl-hillsborough-2026-bocc-d5-hahn-stacy.name: Stacy Hahn
fl-hillsborough-2026-bocc-d5-hahn-stacy.bio: Hillsborough County School Board member since 2018; former University of South Florida College of Education faculty member and public school teacher.

positions.stance: Would protect taxpayers by keeping taxes low, cutting wasteful spending, and improving efficiency inside government first.
Supports law enforcement, strengthening crime prevention, and giving first responders the tools they need.
Would plan for growth by improving roads and transportation, investing in infrastructure, and protecting quality of life.

fl-hillsborough-2026-bocc-d5-manimala-ne.name: Neil Manimala
fl-hillsborough-2026-bocc-d5-manimala-ne.bio: Board-certified urologist and president of the Hillsborough County Medical Association.

positions.stance: Supports workforce development, small business support, affordable housing, childcare access, and apprenticeships.
Would fully resource law enforcement and fire rescue and supports youth diversion and mental health crisis teams.
Supports bus lanes, transit service expansion, crosswalks, and road repair equity.
Prioritizes stormwater drainage, anti-sprawl planning, and hurricane readiness.
Would protect the Hillsborough County Health Care Plan and supports health equity zones and mental health.
